examples.en: My younger sibling drew a cat in the sketchbook.
I went to the stationery store to buy a new sketchbook.

examples.ko: 스케치북이 거의 다 차서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The sketchbook is almost full, so I need to buy a new one.

examples.ko: 이 스케치북은 종이가 두꺼워서 물감을 써도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: This sketchbook has thick paper, so it is fine to use paint.

examples.ko: 아이가 스케치북 한 권을 한 달 만에 다 썼어요.
examples.en: The child used up a whole sketchbook in a month.
I took a sketchbook and colored pencils out of my bag.

explain: 스케치북은 그림을 그리는 공책이에요. 글씨를 쓰거나 문제를 푸는 공책은 '연습장'이나 '공책'이라고 해요. 세는 단위는 '권'이어서 '스케치북 한 권'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: A 스케치북 is for drawing. A notebook for writing or working out problems is called '연습장' or '공책'. You count them with '권', as in '스케치북 한 권'.

examples.en: If you read a lot of books, your expressive ability grows.

examples.ko: 한국어 표현력을 키우고 싶어서 일기를 써요.
examples.en: I want to build my Korean expression skills, so I write a diary.

examples.ko: 표현력은 연습하면 누구나 좋아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can get better at expressing themselves with practice.
To give a good presentation, expressive skill matters too.
I was surprised by the child's expressive ability.

examples.ko: 저는 표현력과 이해력을 함께 기르고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to develop both expressiveness and comprehension.

explain: '표현력이 좋다', '표현력이 풍부하다', '표현력이 늘다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말 '어휘력'은 아는 단어의 양에 가깝고, '표현력'은 생각이나 느낌을 말과 글로 잘 나타내는 힘이에요.
explain_en: It goes with phrases like '표현력이 좋다' and '표현력이 늘다'. The related word '어휘력' is closer to how many words you know, while '표현력' is how well you put thoughts and feelings into speech or writing.

examples.en: In elementary school I memorized the multiplication table like a song.
The multiplication table is the first step in learning multiplication.
These days I sometimes mix up the multiplication table.

examples.ko: 구구단도 잘 못 외우던 제가 지금은 수학을 가르쳐요.
examples.en: I used to be bad even at the times tables, but now I teach math.
I made a bet with a friend using the times tables.
The child finds the seven times table difficult.

explain: 한국에서는 초등학교 때 구구단을 외워요. '이 일은 이, 이 이는 사'처럼 소리 내어 외우고, 2단, 3단처럼 '단'으로 불러요.
explain_en: In Korea children memorize the 구구단 in elementary school, saying it aloud like '이 일은 이, 이 이는 사'. Each table is called a '단', as in 2단 and 3단.

examples.en: Disco was hugely popular in the seventies.

examples.ko: 아버지는 젊었을 때 디스코를 자주 추셨대요.
examples.en: I heard my father often danced disco when he was young.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 디스코 리듬이라서 저절로 몸이 움직여요.
examples.en: This song has a disco rhythm, so my body moves on its own.

examples.ko: 신나는 디스코에 맞춰 다 같이 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: We all danced together to the upbeat disco.

examples.ko: 디스코도 좋지만 저는 발라드가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: Disco is nice, but I like ballads more.

examples.ko: 디스코와 팝송이 많이 나오는 영화를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a movie with a lot of disco and pop songs.

explain: 디스코는 음악도 춤도 가리켜요. 춤은 '추다'와 함께 써서 '디스코를 추다'라고 해요. '디스코 음악', '디스코 리듬'처럼 다른 명사 앞에도 붙여요.
explain_en: 디스코 can mean both the music and the dance. For the dance it pairs with '추다', as in '디스코를 추다'. It also goes before other nouns, like '디스코 음악' and '디스코 리듬'.

examples.en: The child is sucking on a candy.
A mosquito sucked my blood, so my arm itches.
Insects suck the nectar from flowers.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 손가락을 빨아먹는 버릇이 있었어요.
examples.en: As a kid I had a habit of sucking on my fingers.
If you suck on ice, your mouth feels cool.
My younger sibling sucked up all the ice cream.

explain: '빨아먹다'는 입안에서 빨아서 먹는 모습을 그리는 말이에요. 사탕, 꿀, 즙처럼 빨아서 먹는 것과 잘 어울려요. 컵에 든 음료는 보통 '마시다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 사장이 직원들의 피를 빨아먹는다는 기사가 나왔어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 힘들게 번 것을 부당하게 가져가는 사람을 비난할 때 써요. 거친 말이라 일상 대화에서는 조심해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to condemn someone who unfairly takes what others worked hard for. It is harsh, so be careful in daily talk.

explain_en: '빨아먹다' pictures sucking something in your mouth, and it fits things like candy, nectar, or juice. A drink in a cup is usually just '마시다'.

examples.ko: 그 수학자는 오랫동안 어려운 문제를 풀었어요.
examples.en: That mathematician worked on a hard problem for a long time.
My dream is to become a mathematician.
I met a famous mathematician and listened to what they had to say.
The mathematicians gathered and held a meeting.
My uncle is a mathematician, so he loves numbers.
I sent a letter directly to a mathematician.

explain: '-자'는 학문을 하는 사람 뒤에 붙어요. 수학자, 과학자, 철학자처럼요. 학교에서 수학을 가르치는 사람은 '수학 선생님'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: The ending '-자' attaches to people who work in a field of study, as in 수학자, 과학자, and 철학자. Someone who teaches math at school is called a '수학 선생님'.

examples.en: I wrote each Hangul letter ten times in my practice notebook.

examples.ko: 연습장 한 권을 다 쓰고 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I used up a whole practice notebook and bought a new one.
I solve math problems on scratch paper first.
The notebook ran short, so I wrote on the back pages too.
Can I bring a scratch notebook into the exam room?

examples.ko: 이 연습장은 줄이 없어서 그림 그리기에도 좋아요.
examples.en: This notebook has no lines, so it is good for drawing too.

explain: 연습장은 막 써도 되는 공책이에요. 그림을 그리는 공책은 '스케치북', 수업 내용을 정리하는 공책은 그냥 '공책'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A 연습장 is a notebook you can scribble in freely. A drawing pad is a '스케치북', and a notebook for class notes is simply a '공책'.

examples.en: Our school's cheering squad gathered on the field.

examples.ko: 응원단은 경기 내내 큰 소리로 노래했어요.
examples.en: The cheering squad sang loudly throughout the game.
I was in the cheering squad in college.
The players took a photo with the cheering squad.
I saw a poster saying they are recruiting for the cheering squad.

examples.ko: 빨간 옷을 입은 응원단 덕분에 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the cheering squad in red, I felt energized.

explain: 응원단은 모임 전체를 말하고, 응원하는 행동은 '응원하다'라고 해요. 응원단에 속한 한 사람은 '응원단원'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 응원단 names the whole group, while '응원하다' is the action of cheering. One member of the squad is called a '응원단원'.

examples.en: There is a small village on the far side of the river.
Someone over there is waving a hand.
The sun slowly set behind the mountain.
The other side of the road is still under construction.
What kind of country might be across the sea?

examples.ko: 안개가 짙어서 저편이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The fog is thick, so I can't see the far side well.

explain: '이편'과 '저편'은 짝이에요. 말하는 사람에게서 먼 쪽이 저편이고, 가까운 쪽이 이편이에요. 같은 상황에 '저쪽'도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '이편' and '저편' are a pair: 저편 is the side far from the speaker and 이편 is the near side. '저쪽' can also be used in the same situation.

examples.ko: 타임머신이 있다면 과거로 가 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: If there were a time machine, I would like to go to the past.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 타임머신을 타고 미래로 갔어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the hero rode a time machine to the future.

examples.ko: 타임머신 같은 건 현실에는 아직 없어요.
examples.en: Things like time machines don't exist in reality yet.
I want to go back to my childhood by time machine.
My friend lent me a book about time machines.
We don't even have a time machine, so how can we go back to yesterday?

explain: '타임머신을 타다'처럼 '타다'와 함께 써요. 오래된 물건이나 사진을 보고 옛날로 돌아간 느낌이 들면 '타임머신을 탄 것 같아요'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '타다', as in '타임머신을 타다'. When an old photo or object makes you feel you went back in time, people say '타임머신을 탄 것 같아요'.

examples.en: In spring, tulips bloomed fully in the park.
I gave my mother red tulips as a gift.
Tulips come in many colors, so the flower bed is colorful.
We took a family photo in front of the tulip field.

examples.ko: 튤립과 장미 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like more, tulips or roses?
The Netherlands is a country famous for tulips.

explain: '튤립이 피다'처럼 꽃이 필 때는 '피다'를 써요. 꽃을 세는 단위는 '송이'여서 '튤립 한 송이'라고 말해요.
explain_en: For blooming, say '튤립이 피다' with '피다'. Flowers are counted with '송이', as in '튤립 한 송이'.

examples.ko: 나뭇잎 위에 애벌레가 천천히 기어가고 있어요.
examples.en: A caterpillar is crawling slowly across the leaf.
A caterpillar goes through a chrysalis and becomes a butterfly.
I was startled to find a caterpillar in the cabbage field.
The child gave leaves to the caterpillar as food.
I get goosebumps just from seeing a caterpillar.

examples.ko: 초록색 애벌레 한 마리가 창문에 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A green caterpillar is stuck to the window.

explain: 곤충은 '마리'로 세요. '애벌레 한 마리', '애벌레 두 마리'처럼 말해요. 나비의 애벌레처럼 어떤 곤충인지 말하고 싶을 때는 '나비 애벌레'라고 앞에 이름을 붙여요.
explain_en: Insects are counted with '마리', as in '애벌레 한 마리'. To say which insect it belongs to, put the name before it, like '나비 애벌레'.

examples.ko: 어두운 방에 혼자 있으니 무서움이 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: Being alone in the dark room, fear washed over me.
I turned on the light to overcome my fear.

examples.ko: 아이는 무서움에 떨며 엄마 곁에 붙어 있었어요.
examples.en: The child clung to its mother, trembling with fear.
Fear is a feeling everyone has.
The movie was so fun that I even forgot my fear.

examples.ko: 그는 무서움 없이 혼자 숲으로 들어갔어요.
examples.en: He went into the forest alone without any fear.

explain: '무서움을 느끼다', '무서움을 이기다'처럼 써요. '무섭다'에서 나온 명사예요. 무서움은 귀신, 어둠, 높은 곳처럼 눈앞의 것이 무서울 때 쓰고, '두려움'은 앞으로 일어날 일이 걱정될 때도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요.

phrases.example: 동생은 무서움을 많이 타서 밤에 혼자 화장실에 못 가요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁이 많아서 쉽게 무서워하는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 여기서 '타다'는 그런 느낌을 잘 받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who gets scared easily. Here '타다' means being prone to that feeling.

explain_en: It goes with '무서움을 느끼다' and '무서움을 이기다', and it is the noun form of '무섭다'. 무서움 is for something scary right in front of you, like ghosts, the dark or heights, while '두려움' is wider and also covers worry about what may happen.

examples.en: I stepped in dog droppings on the street and my shoes got dirty.
You put dog droppings in a bag and throw them in the trash.
There was a lot of dog mess in the park, so I walked carefully.

examples.ko: 창문을 열었더니 개똥 냄새가 나서 닫았어요.
examples.en: I opened the window, smelled dog droppings, and closed it.
I almost slipped on dog droppings without noticing.
A puppy left dog droppings in the park.

explain: '소똥', '말똥'처럼 동물 이름 뒤에 '똥'을 붙여요. 사람이 눈 것은 그냥 '똥'이라고 해요. 똥은 거친 말은 아니지만 밥 먹을 때 꺼내기는 조심해요.

phrases.example: 평소에는 흔하던 우산이 비 오는 날엔 하나도 안 보여요. 개똥도 약에 쓰려면 없다더니 그 말이 맞네요.
phrases.en: Even dog dung is nowhere to be found when you need it as medicine
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소에 흔하던 것도 막상 필요해서 찾으면 없을 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb for when something that was everywhere suddenly cannot be found once you need it.
phrases.en_equiv: You can never find it when you need it.

explain_en: Animal droppings are named by putting the animal first, like '소똥' and '말똥'. A person's is just '똥'. It is not rude, but people avoid bringing it up while eating.

examples.en: We raised our juice glasses and made a toast.
I make a toast to the new year with friends.
We all toasted and then ate cake.
The boss suggested that we toast first.

examples.ko: 축하하는 마음으로 건배하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see them toasting with congratulations in their hearts.
Is everyone ready to make a toast?

explain: 건배할 때는 '건배!'나 '위하여!'라고 외쳐요. 무엇을 위해 건배하는지는 '새해를 위하여'처럼 '-을/를 위하여'로 말해요.
explain_en: When toasting, people shout '건배!' or '위하여!'. To say what the toast is for, use '-을/를 위하여', as in '새해를 위하여'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 도둑질을 하면 안 된다고 배웠어요.
examples.en: As a child I learned that stealing is wrong.
Theft is a serious crime, so you get punished.

examples.ko: 가게에서 도둑질이 자주 일어나서 카메라를 달았어요.
examples.en: Thefts kept happening in the shop, so they installed a camera.

examples.ko: 도둑질로 잡혀 간 사람이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A person arrested for theft appeared on the news.
The villagers are anxious because of the thefts.
The punishment for theft is very strict.

explain: 행동은 '도둑질', 사람은 '도둑'이에요. 도둑에게 물건을 빼앗긴 쪽은 '도둑을 맞다', '도둑맞다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: The act is '도둑질' and the person is '도둑'. Someone whose things were taken by a thief says '도둑을 맞다' or '도둑맞다'.

examples.en: The child regretted having stolen from the store.
He was so hungry that he stole some bread.
If you steal other people's things, you get punished.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어제 옆집에서 도둑질하다가 잡혔어요.
examples.en: That person was caught yesterday while stealing from the next-door house.

examples.ko: 도둑질해서 번 돈은 쓰고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to spend money earned by stealing.
Don't steal; that belongs to your friend.

explain: '훔치다'는 '지갑을 훔치다'처럼 물건 하나를 몰래 가져가는 행동이에요. '도둑질하다'는 도둑 같은 짓을 한다는 느낌이 강해서 나쁜 행동이라고 말하는 분위기가 있어요. '도둑질을 하다'처럼 나누어 쓸 수도 있어요.
explain_en: '훔치다' is quietly taking one item, as in '지갑을 훔치다'. '도둑질하다' has the feel of doing what a thief does, so it carries a tone of calling the act bad. It can also be split as '도둑질을 하다'.

examples.en: I failed the exam and I am so upset.
I did not pass this interview.

examples.ko: 한 번 불합격해도 다시 도전하면 돼요.
examples.en: Even if you fail once, you can try again.
What should I do if I fail?
I comforted a friend who failed the driving test.

examples.ko: 불합격할까 봐 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep all night, afraid that I might fail.

explain: 반대말은 '합격하다'예요. 대화에서는 '시험에 떨어지다'라고도 말해요. 결과를 말할 때는 '불합격이에요'처럼 '이다'를 붙여 써도 돼요.
explain_en: The opposite is '합격하다'. In conversation people also say '시험에 떨어지다'. For a result you can also say '불합격이에요' with '이다'.

examples.en: It rained a lot around this time last year too.
When this time of year comes, I think of my hometown.
Around this time, cherry blossoms start to bloom.
By this time next year, I want to be good at Korean.
Every year around this time I travel with my family.
The sky at this time of year is especially clear.

explain: '작년 이맘때', '내년 이맘때'처럼 해마다 돌아오는 같은 시기를 말할 때 써요. 지금 이 순간을 말할 때는 '지금'이나 '이때'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for the same point in a recurring cycle, as in '작년 이맘때' and '내년 이맘때'. For this very moment, say '지금' or '이때'.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에 과속하면 아주 위험해요.
examples.en: Speeding on a rainy day is very dangerous.

examples.ko: 아버지는 운전할 때 절대 과속하지 않으세요.
examples.en: My father never speeds when he drives.
The car was speeding and got caught by the police.
Yesterday I saw a speeding car on the highway.
I almost had an accident because I was speeding.
I was worried my friend might speed.

explain: 도로의 제한 속도를 넘어 달릴 때 써요. 명사 '과속'에 다른 말을 붙여 '과속 운전', '과속 단속'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when driving over the speed limit. The noun '과속' also combines with other words, as in '과속 운전' and '과속 단속'.

examples.en: At the wedding, the bride threw the bouquet.
The bouquet was made beautifully with white roses.
The bouquet the bride is holding is really pretty.
I heard the groom picked out the bouquet himself too.
I tied a small ribbon on the bouquet.

examples.ko: 부케 던지기 행사를 할 때 모두 웃었어요.
examples.en: Everyone laughed during the bouquet toss.

explain: '꽃다발'은 모든 꽃 묶음을 가리키고, '부케'는 주로 결혼식에서 신부가 드는 꽃다발에 써요. '부케를 던지다', '부케를 받다'처럼 써요. 부케를 받은 사람이 다음에 결혼한다는 말이 있어요.
explain_en: '꽃다발' covers any bunch of flowers, while '부케' is mainly the bunch a bride holds at a wedding. Say '부케를 던지다' (throw) and '부케를 받다' (catch). There is a saying that whoever catches it will marry next.

examples.en: I want to work at an import-export company.
Trade declined this year, so the port is quiet.
The two countries promised to increase trade.
Imports and exports are very important to a country's economy.
This document is absolutely necessary for importing and exporting.
The scale of trade is growing every year.

explain: '수출'은 물건을 나라 밖으로 내보내는 일, '수입'은 안으로 들여오는 일이에요. 두 가지를 함께 말할 때 '수출입'이라고 하고, 한쪽만 말할 때는 '수출'이나 '수입'을 써요.
explain_en: '수출' is sending goods out of the country and '수입' is bringing them in. '수출입' covers both together, and for just one side you say '수출' or '수입'.

examples.en: If breathing is hard, please open the window.
I practice breathing before I exercise.
Breathing is very important for health.
I have a cold, so even breathing is uncomfortable.
If you breathe slowly, your mind relaxes.
Breathing and walking are the easiest exercises.

explain: '숨쉬기 운동'처럼 연습이나 운동 이름 앞에 잘 붙어요. 아파서 숨 쉬기 힘들 때는 '숨이 차다', '숨이 막히다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It attaches easily before names of practice or exercise, as in '숨쉬기 운동'. When it is hard to breathe because of illness, say '숨이 차다' or '숨이 막히다'.

examples.en: I clipped and saved a newspaper article.
I save good articles and read them later.
I keep my articles in a clipping folder.

examples.ko: 이 게시물을 스크랩하면 내 보관함에 저장돼요.
examples.en: If you save this post, it is stored in my archive.

examples.ko: 스크랩한 글이 너무 많아서 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: I have too many saved articles and need to organize them.

examples.ko: 인터넷 기사 스크랩은 숙제에 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: Saving internet articles helped with my homework.

explain: 신문이나 잡지에서 필요한 기사를 오려 모으는 일이에요. 요즘은 인터넷 글을 저장하는 일도 '스크랩'이라고 하고, 동사는 '스크랩하다'예요.
explain_en: It means cutting out articles from newspapers or magazines and keeping them. Today it also means saving online posts, and the verb is '스크랩하다'.

examples.en: Draw a diagonal line in the rectangle.
Don't cross the road diagonally.
The two diagonals meet in the middle.
Which diagonal is longer?
I folded the paper diagonally to make a triangle.

examples.ko: 대각선에 있는 가게가 우리 집 단골 식당이에요.
examples.en: The shop diagonally across is our regular restaurant.

explain: 수학에서는 사각형의 마주 보는 꼭짓점을 이은 선을 말해요. 일상에서는 '대각선 방향', '대각선 맞은편'처럼 비스듬한 방향이나 자리를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: In math it is the line joining opposite corners of a quadrilateral. In daily life it also marks a slanted direction or spot, as in '대각선 방향' and '대각선 맞은편'.

examples.ko: 이 베이지 코트가 저한테 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This beige coat suits me well.
Beige goes well with any color.
I painted the wall beige, and the room got brighter.
Yesterday I bought a pair of beige pants.
It is a bag mixing white and beige.

examples.ko: 베이지도 좋지만 저는 검은색이 더 편해요.
examples.en: Beige is nice too, but I feel more comfortable in black.

explain: 색 이름은 '베이지색'처럼 '색'을 붙여도 되고, '베이지 코트'처럼 바로 명사 앞에 써도 돼요. '핑크'나 '민트' 같은 외래어 색 이름도 같은 방식으로 써요.
explain_en: You can add '색' as in '베이지색', or put it straight before a noun as in '베이지 코트'. Loanword color names like '핑크' and '민트' work the same way.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 전 세계에서 수억 명이 봤어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of millions of people around the world watched this movie.
I heard that painting sold for hundreds of millions of won.

examples.ko: 목성은 지구에서 수억 킬로미터나 떨어져 있어요.
examples.en: Jupiter is hundreds of millions of kilometers away from Earth.
Hundreds of millions of years ago, dinosaurs lived.
Hundreds of millions of fish live in the sea.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 수억 번 들어도 질리지 않아요.
examples.en: I never get tired of this song even after hearing it hundreds of millions of times.

explain: '수억 원', '수억 명'처럼 단위 앞에 바로 붙여요. 정확한 숫자는 모르지만 억이 여러 개 되는 아주 큰 수를 말할 때 써요. '수십', '수백', '수천', '수만'도 같은 방식으로 써요.
explain_en: It attaches directly before a unit, as in '수억 원' and '수억 명'. The exact number is unknown, but it is several hundred million. '수십', '수백', '수천', and '수만' work the same way.

examples.en: I put a lot of toppings on the pizza.
Which topping is the tastiest?
I'll have chocolate as the ice cream topping.
Adding a topping costs one thousand won.
You can pick the toppings yourself too.
If you add fruit as a topping, it is fresher.

explain: '토핑을 올리다', '토핑을 추가하다'처럼 써요. 한식에서 음식 위에 얹는 것은 '고명'이라고 부르고, 피자나 아이스크림처럼 서양식 음식에는 '토핑'을 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with '토핑을 올리다' and '토핑을 추가하다'. What goes on top of Korean dishes is called '고명', while '토핑' is used for things like pizza and ice cream.

examples.en: The child fell asleep early in pajamas.
The pajamas were so comfy that I wore them all day.
I went to the convenience store in my pajamas.
The new pajamas are cotton, so they are very soft.

examples.ko: 파자마도 챙겼어요? 오늘 자고 갈 거잖아요.
examples.en: Did you pack pajamas too? You're staying over tonight.
I accidentally spilled coffee on my pajamas.

explain: '잠옷'은 잘 때 입는 옷 전체를 말해요. 파자마는 그중에서 윗옷과 바지가 따로 있는 옷을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '잠옷' covers any clothes worn for sleeping. 파자마 is the kind with a separate top and pants.

examples.en: I am studying Korean studies at university.
The Korean studies class is really fun.

examples.ko: 한국학은 역사와 문화를 함께 배우는 학문이에요.
examples.en: Korean studies is a field where you learn history and culture together.

examples.ko: 한국학에 관심이 많은 외국 학생이 늘었어요.
examples.en: There are more foreign students interested in Korean studies.

examples.ko: 한국학도 이제 전 세계에서 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can now study Korean studies all over the world.
Our university has newly opened a Korean studies department.

explain: '-학'은 학문 이름에 붙어요. 한국학, 중국학, 일본학처럼 한 나라를 연구하는 학문에 써요. 한국어 자체를 연구하는 분야는 '한국어학'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The ending '-학' marks a field of study, as in 한국학, 중국학, and 일본학. The study of the Korean language itself is called '한국어학'.

examples.ko: 이 생수에는 미네랄이 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This bottled water contains a lot of minerals.

examples.ko: 미네랄을 따로 챙겨 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people take minerals separately.
I bought a bottle of mineral water at the mart.
Minerals are nutrients the body definitely needs.

examples.ko: 미네랄도 비타민처럼 음식으로 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Like vitamins, you can get minerals from food.

examples.ko: 이 화장품에는 미네랄 성분이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This cosmetic contains mineral ingredients.

explain: 건강 이야기에서는 '비타민과 미네랄'처럼 짝을 이루어 말해요. 생수는 '미네랄워터'라고도 해요.
explain_en: In talk about health it often appears as a pair, '비타민과 미네랄'. Bottled water is also called '미네랄워터'.

examples.en: I made a pancake with garlic chives in it.

examples.ko: 부추는 향이 강해서 한 번에 조금만 넣어요.
examples.en: Garlic chives have a strong aroma, so I add only a little at a time.
These dumplings have garlic chives in them.
I bought a bunch of garlic chives at the mart.
Try adding a little garlic chives to the soup too.
On rainy days I think of garlic chive pancakes.

explain: 부추는 가늘고 납작한 잎이에요. '대파'는 굵고 하얀 줄기가 있는 다른 채소예요. 다발은 '단'으로 세요.
explain_en: 부추 has thin, flat leaves, unlike '대파', which has a thick white stalk. A bunch is counted with '단'.

examples.en: I hear a bell ringing from far away.
I took a walk listening to the church bell.
I woke up startled by the sound of a bell.
The school bell is a signal that class is over.
On New Year's we make wishes along with the sound of the bell.
It is a quiet village where not even a bell can be heard.

explain: '종소리가 울리다', '종소리가 들리다'처럼 써요. 종은 '치다'나 '울리다'와 함께 써서 '종을 치다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It goes with '종소리가 울리다' and '종소리가 들리다'. The bell itself pairs with '치다' or '울리다', as in '종을 치다'.

examples.en: My back hurt, so I saw a traditional Korean medicine doctor.

examples.ko: 한의사는 맥을 짚고 몸 상태를 살펴봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor took my pulse and checked my condition.
My aunt works as a traditional Korean medicine doctor.
The doctor gave me acupuncture.
I asked the doctor about teas that are good for the body.
A traditional Korean medicine doctor is also a medical professional who sees patients.

explain: 병원에서 진료하는 사람은 '의사', 한의원에서 진료하는 사람은 '한의사'라고 해요. 한의사가 일하는 곳은 '한의원'이에요.
explain_en: A doctor at a hospital is an '의사', while one at a traditional Korean clinic is a '한의사'. The place where a 한의사 works is a '한의원'.

examples.en: I made a new friend who is the same age as me.
Since we were all the same age, we talked comfortably.
That actor is the same age as me.
I went on a trip to Jeju with friends my age.
We are the same age, so we became close quickly.
Meeting someone my age abroad makes me really happy.

explain: '동갑'과 같은 뜻으로, 친근하게 부를 때 '동갑내기'라고 해요. '-내기'는 '시골내기', '신출내기'처럼 사람 뒤에 붙는 말이에요. 한국에서는 나이로 말투를 정하는 일이 있어서 동갑인지 먼저 묻기도 해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '동갑' but sounds friendlier. The ending '-내기' attaches to people, as in '시골내기' and '신출내기'. In Korea speech style can depend on age, so people sometimes ask first whether you are 동갑.

examples.en: This watch is a little inaccurate with the time.
You shouldn't trust inaccurate information.

examples.ko: 그 기사는 내용이 부정확해서 다시 고쳤어요.
examples.en: The article's content was inaccurate, so it was corrected.
Isn't my pronunciation imprecise?

examples.ko: 부정확하게 말하면 오해가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak imprecisely, misunderstandings can arise.
The map must have been inaccurate, because I got lost.

explain: 반대말은 '정확하다'예요. '정확하지 않다'라고 풀어서 말해도 같은 뜻이에요. '틀리다'는 아예 맞지 않다는 뜻이라서, 대체로 맞지만 어딘가 모자랄 때는 '부정확하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '정확하다', and '정확하지 않다' says the same thing in two words. '틀리다' means completely wrong, so for something that is mostly right but not exact, use '부정확하다'.

examples.en: Applicants must write their name and the date.
There were too many applicants, so we decided by lottery.
Please check the applicants for this lecture.
I sent a text message to the applicants.
We give a small gift to applicants.
We chose three people from among the applicants.

explain: '-자'가 붙어 사람을 나타내요. 신청한 사람은 '신청자', 참가하는 사람은 '참가자', 지원하는 사람은 '지원자'예요. 신청하는 일은 '신청하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The ending '-자' marks a person: '신청자' applied, '참가자' participates, and '지원자' volunteers or applies for a job. The action is '신청하다'.

examples.en: The hospital director met the patient in person.
I greeted the hospital director.
The newly arrived director has a reputation for being kind.
To see the hospital director, you must make an appointment.
The hospital director and the doctors held a meeting together.
Everyone listened quietly to the director's words.

explain: '-장'은 어떤 곳의 책임자 이름에 붙어요. 학교는 '교장', 병원은 '병원장', 회사는 '사장'처럼 곳마다 말이 달라요. 높여 부를 때는 '님'을 붙여 '병원장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The ending '-장' marks the head of a place, and each place has its own word: '교장' for a school, '병원장' for a hospital, '사장' for a company. To show respect add '님', as in '병원장님'.

examples.ko: 아버지는 한 달에 한 번 이발하세요.
examples.en: My father gets a haircut once a month.
I am going to get a haircut on the weekend.
My hair was long, so I got a haircut yesterday.
After the haircut, I feel refreshed.
I have to get a haircut before graduation.
It hasn't been long since I got a haircut.

explain: '이발하다'와 '머리를 자르다'는 둘 다 머리카락을 자를 때 써요. 이발하는 곳은 '이발소'예요. 미용실에서는 보통 '머리 자르러 왔어요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Both '이발하다' and '머리를 자르다' are used for cutting hair. The place for it is an '이발소'. At a salon people usually say '머리 자르러 왔어요'.

examples.en: I am the second son among three brothers.
The second son is much taller than his older brother.
The neighbors' second son is getting married this fall.

examples.ko: 차남인 저는 형과 성격이 많이 달라요.
examples.en: As the second son, my personality is very different from my brother's.
I was introduced to the boss's second son.
My parents gave the second son the same allowance too.

explain: 아들의 순서는 '장남, 차남, 삼남'이라고 해요. 딸은 '장녀, 차녀, 삼녀'예요. 가장 어린 아들은 '막내아들'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: Sons are ranked '장남, 차남, 삼남', and daughters '장녀, 차녀, 삼녀'. The youngest son can also be called '막내아들'.

examples.en: I caught a cold and my nostrils are blocked.
Don't pick your nose in front of people.

examples.ko: 아이가 콧구멍에 콩을 넣어서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The child put a bean in its nostril, so we went to the hospital.
Try breathing slowly through your nostrils.
A person has two nostrils.
When I wash my face, I clean my nostrils well too.

explain: '코'와 '구멍' 사이에 'ㅅ'이 들어가 '콧구멍'이 돼요. 발음은 [코꾸멍]이에요. '콧물'도 같은 방식으로 만들어진 말이에요.
explain_en: An 'ㅅ' is inserted between '코' and '구멍' to form '콧구멍', pronounced [코꾸멍]. '콧물' is formed the same way.

examples.en: I couldn't do my homework because of laziness.
Stop being lazy and get up quickly.

examples.ko: 아침마다 게으름이 저를 이불 속에 붙잡아요.
examples.en: Every morning laziness keeps me in my blanket.
Everyone has a bit of laziness.
I exercise every day to get out of laziness.
On weekends a little laziness is sometimes needed too.

explain: '게으름을 피우다', '게으름을 부리다'처럼 써요. 사람의 성격을 말할 때는 형용사 '게으르다'를 쓰는데, '게을러요'처럼 모양이 바뀌는 르 불규칙이에요.
explain_en: It pairs with '게으름을 피우다' and '게으름을 부리다'. To describe a person use the adjective '게으르다', which is a 르-irregular adjective and becomes '게을러요'.

examples.ko: 직원이 친절히 알려 줘서 길을 쉽게 찾았어요.
examples.en: The staff member kindly told me, so I found the way easily.

examples.ko: 선생님은 제 질문에 친절히 대답해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher kindly answered my question.
You should treat even strangers kindly.
I kindly gave up my seat to the grandmother.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 약 먹는 법을 친절히 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor kindly explained how to take the medicine.

examples.ko: 손님을 친절히 맞이하는 가게가 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Shops that welcome customers kindly are popular.

explain: '친절하다'에서 나온 부사예요. '친절하게'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, '친절히'는 조금 글 같은 느낌이 나요. 같은 방식으로 '조용하다'는 '조용히'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is the adverb from '친절하다' and means almost the same as '친절하게', though '친절히' sounds a little more written. The same pattern turns '조용하다' into '조용히'.

examples.en: Snow blossoms covered the winter mountain.

examples.ko: 주말에 눈꽃을 보러 태백산에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: This weekend I am going to Taebaeksan to see the snow-covered trees.
Snow blossoms sparkle in the sunlight.
A snow blossom festival is being held, so there are many people.
She wore a dress as white as snow blossoms.

examples.ko: 눈꽃과 함께 찍은 사진이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The photo taken with the snow blossoms is really pretty.

explain: '눈꽃이 피다'처럼 눈이 나뭇가지에 하얗게 쌓인 모습을 꽃에 빗대어 말해요. 하늘에서 내리는 눈 한 알 한 알은 '눈송이'라고 해요.
explain_en: '눈꽃이 피다' compares snow piled white on branches to flowers in bloom. Each flake falling from the sky is a '눈송이'.
